A Lorentz force levitation method based on artificial magnetic field - China patent 

#ufotwitter

The invention utilizes a "master" spacecraft (hosting an artificial magnetic field) and a "secondary" (slave) spacecraft that carries an electric charge. By manipulating the Lorentz force generated between the two, the system maintains the secondary craft in a fixed position relative to the primary one—essentially acting as a propellant-free suspension system.

Key Technical Features

Arbitrary Positioning: Unlike previous techniques that were limited to specific equilibrium points (e.g., along basic radial, tangential, or normal axes), this method allows for suspension at essentially any relative position.

Mechanism:

Artificial Magnetic Field: The master satellite is equipped with three orthogonal superconducting coils.

Current Regulation: The direction and intensity of the artificial magnetic field are precisely controlled by adjusting the current in these three coils.
Dynamic Adjustment: The suspension position can be fine-tuned further by altering the electric charge on the secondary satellite.

Fuel Efficiency: Because the system relies on Lorentz force interaction rather than chemical propulsion to maintain the formation, it operates without consuming propellant, which eliminates contamination—an important factor for sensitive optical equipment like cameras.

Why This Is Different

Usually, when we think of "levitation," we think of Meissner effect (superconductors hovering over magnets) or simple permanent magnets. Those are static—they don't allow you to move the object around easily or hold it at an arbitrary distance without a track.

This patent is essentially Dynamic Magnetic Positioning. By tuning the currents in the coils, you aren't just locking an object in place; you are defining the exact coordinates $(x, y, z)$ in 3D space where the object will hover. If you want the satellite to drift slightly to the left or move closer to the camera lens, you simply adjust the current, and the "equilibrium point" (the bottom of the magnetic bowl) shifts accordingly.

Practical Implications

This removes the "slop" and vibration associated with mechanical arms or chemical thrusters. For space-based observation, this means:

Precision Stability: You can hold a camera or a sensor at a specific standoff distance with extreme steadiness because you aren't fighting the plume of a thruster.

Infinite Persistence: As long as you have power for the superconducting coils, you don't "run out of gas."

Multi-Mission Flexibility: The same hardware can be used to hold different satellites at different distances for different missions just by changing the software control parameters.
